characters.name: Abel
characters.art_alt: Abel from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Abel is a well-rounded melee character who possesses a terrifyingly amazing mixup game.

characters.name: Adon
characters.art_alt: Adon from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: With meter, Projectiles mean nothing to Adon, he possesses an instant overhead at any time with EX Air Jaguar kick, multiple armor breaking moves with or without meter meaning focus attacks mean nothing to him.

characters.name: Akuma
characters.art_alt: Akuma from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Akuma's vortex game is absolutely unparalleled, and is practically the defining point of his playstyle.

characters.name: Balrog
characters.art_alt: Balrog from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Balrog's anti-air option are very good, and he can play an excellent mixup/footsie game as well.

characters.name: Blanka
characters.art_alt: Blanka from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Blanka is a tricky character who, despite being a charge character, has deadly mixup potential.

characters.name: C. Viper
characters.art_alt: C. Viper from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: C. Viper's mix-up is absolutely devastating, being able to cross up with Aerial Burn Kicks mixed in with safe Overheads and super jump cancels, which she can use to combo into her Ultras for well over 50% of the opponent's health bar.

characters.name: Cammy
characters.art_alt: Cammy from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Cammy is a fast, rushdown-oriented character who is very tricky to play and fight against.

characters.name: Chun-Li
characters.art_alt: Chun-Li from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Chun-Li is a technical, but well-rounded character who can do relatively well in almost any situation.

characters.name: Cody
characters.art_alt: Cody from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: The moment he gains momentum in a match, he can and will keep you under constant pressure, waiting for that one opportunity to tick throw or punish should your guard be broken down.

characters.name: Dan
characters.art_alt: Dan from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Dan is a gameplay-focused Ultra Street Fighter IV fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Decapre
characters.art_alt: Decapre from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Decapre's execution is a bit challenging with some strict charge times and quick piano inputs, but she is rewarded with high damage and consistent frame trap pressure.

characters.name: Dee Jay
characters.art_alt: Dee Jay from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: With no room for your opponent to back up, they will be much more susceptible to being hit by Dee Jay's attacks, which will have more combo potential and mix-up ambiguity.

characters.name: Dhalsim
characters.art_alt: Dhalsim from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: With his Yoga Fire and extremely slow jump, Dhalsim can also fake out his opponents with a sudden Yoga Teleport that can potentially lead into a shocking mixup.

characters.name: Dudley
characters.art_alt: Dudley from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Because everything can lead into a comboed EX Machine Gun Punch, whether it's a low hitting Crouching Light Kick or the quick Overhead of Towards Hard Kick, the pressure Dudley can sustain on an opponent is nigh overwhelming, and a dizzy is almost guaranteed after two mix-ups, making Dudley truly a terror once he gets in.

characters.name: E. Honda
characters.art_alt: E. Honda from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: If he gets in close enough, Honda can also make you respect his Oicho Throw, which has excellent invincibility for a command grab.

characters.name: El Fuerte
characters.art_alt: El Fuerte from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Requiring a large amount of dexterity, Fuerte also requires a high level of mind games in being able to continually mix your opponents up over and over again with his armada of Habanero Dash attacks.

characters.name: Elena
characters.art_alt: Elena from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Elena also has a monstrous mixup game with meter; any cancellable normal can be followed up with EX Mallet Smash, a near unreactable overhead that grants a followup combo, or Lynx Tail, a multi-hit low that knocks down and can FADC for big damage.

characters.name: Evil Ryu
characters.art_alt: Evil Ryu from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: In terms of defense, however, he becomes very reliant on his Shoryuken, as his teleport is very slow in comparison to Akuma's, and some of his normals (especially his Crouching Medium Kick, Crouching Heavy Punch, and Crouching Heavy Kick) are not as fast as Ryu's.

characters.name: Fei Long
characters.art_alt: Fei Long from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Fei Long's Shienkyaku is an excellent wakeup move as well as an excellent anti-air.

characters.name: Gen
characters.art_alt: Gen from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Without learning how to perform Standing Medium Kick into Hands or the proper distances or cross-up Oga Wall Dive kicks, for example, using Gen may be a losing battle.

characters.name: Gouken
characters.art_alt: Gouken from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Gouken is a gameplay-focused Ultra Street Fighter IV fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Guile
characters.art_alt: Guile from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Not only does it cover a wide area that forces the opponent to either jump, focus absorb, or block, but thanks to Guile's exclusive charge timing being shorter than everyone else's, he can both bombard and condition the opponent with them.

characters.name: Guy
characters.art_alt: Guy from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Not only can he be tricky to fight against, dealing with his "cross-up or not" mix-ups using Jumping Medium Kick and the Elbow Drop or dealing with his Run pressure up close or getting grabbed by surprise Bushin Throws, he's also a very tricky character to learn.

characters.name: Hakan
characters.art_alt: Hakan from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Starting with the AE 2012 update, Hakan now starts every round in Oil Mode, which, in addition to giving him a huge boost in mobility and power, also gives him incredible grab range, a small defense boost (causing every hit he takes to inflict less damage), and the deadly ability to cancel both of his dashes into his normals!

characters.name: Hugo
characters.art_alt: Hugo from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: A good Hugo player knows how to use Hugo's massive size to effectively control their opponent's space, acting as a moving wall that pushes them towards the corner, where there is little chance of escape.

characters.name: Ibuki
characters.art_alt: Ibuki from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: One thing that makes Ibuki so unique is her mobility.

characters.name: Juri
characters.art_alt: Juri from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Juri is a tricky character who excels in the three "M"s of the fighting game world - mobility, mixup, and mind games.

characters.name: Ken
characters.art_alt: Ken from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Ken is one of the few characters who have the ability to kara-throw, making him even deadlier when he's not quite in the range you think he can catch you.

characters.name: M. Bison
characters.art_alt: M. Bison from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Your goal with Bison will be to bully your adversaries with pokes and pressure, and whittle away at them slowly but steadily, breaking their mental guard through frustration and conditioning.

characters.name: Makoto
characters.art_alt: Makoto from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Makoto's awkward Dash and extremely slow walk speed can make for a very difficult character to learn, making it very hard to control your distances from the opponent.

characters.name: Oni
characters.art_alt: Oni from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Oni's only reliable option for a reversal is the Shoryuken, and despite him having higher health than Akuma, he is also bulkier, having sub-par walk speed and a horrible backdash to boot.

characters.name: Poison
characters.art_alt: Poison from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Poison can also throw out a slow, nearly stationary projectile that gives great frame advantage if the opponent doesn't interrupt its startup.

characters.name: R. Mika
characters.art_alt: R. Mika from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: R. Mika loves harassing the opponent with her great normals, a command grab that loops into itself, and great mobility.

characters.name: Rufus
characters.art_alt: Rufus from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: The epitome of the Dive Kick character, Rufus's strength lies almost entirely in his Dive Kick game.

characters.name: Ryu
characters.art_alt: Ryu from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Ryu has all the basic tools you need: great normals, a projectile, an effective anti-air, Focus Attack Dash Cancel (FADC) combos, etc.

characters.name: Sagat
characters.art_alt: Sagat from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Sagat is a zoning character who specializes in confusing his opponents with his unique high/low fireball mixup, then punishing the opponent when they think they have room to breathe.

characters.name: Sakura
characters.art_alt: Sakura from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: What she gets in return is absurd frame data, looping vortex, and enough damage to always be a knockdown away from stealing a round.

characters.name: Seth
characters.art_alt: Seth from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Seth is a gameplay-focused Ultra Street Fighter IV fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: T. Hawk
characters.art_alt: T. Hawk from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Wait for your opponent to make a mistake and condition them with fake-outs and pokes to divert their attention as you go in for a command grab.

characters.name: Vega
characters.art_alt: Vega from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Vega specializes in playing patiently while using his mobility and excellent pokes to scare and enrage the opponent into making fatal mistakes, then punishing them for their insolence.

characters.name: Yang
characters.art_alt: Yang from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Yang is a gameplay-focused Ultra Street Fighter IV fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Yun
characters.art_alt: Yun from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: Even after the nerfs brought in 2012, Yun still has a devastating mixup game with his Dive Kicks, Flip Grabs, and hard-hitting high-low combos, as well as his Palms, which can be either feinted or used to build meter in addition for attacking.

characters.name: Zangief
characters.art_alt: Zangief from Ultra Street Fighter IV
characters.description: While the fear of his dreaded Spinning Piledriver is natural, Zangief players must also make their opponents fear his other useful tools, such as the Banishing Flat, which eats up non-EX/Super/Ultra/flaming fireballs and sets him up for a free Jab Piledriver if within range.

characters.name: Annie
characters.art_alt: Annie from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Annie's special feature is Star Power, a super that improves a variety of Annie's attacks, making her a lot more versatile for combos and pressure and extremely dangerous in neutral.

characters.name: Beowulf
characters.art_alt: Beowulf from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Beowulf is best at close range utilizing his fast hop-dash overheads to force his opponent to guess between a high/low/throw.

characters.name: Big Band
characters.art_alt: Big Band from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Big Band has a variety of large moves that can control most of the screen, and has simple but effective mixup that leads to high damage.

characters.name: Black Dahlia
characters.art_alt: Black Dahlia from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Whilst her overall damage is on the lower end, creative use of her full suite of options opens up complex setplay, neutral and pressure situations.

characters.name: Cerebella
characters.art_alt: Cerebella from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Cerebella is a grappler with a diverse tool-kit and has excellent hurtboxes/hitboxes on many of her normals.

characters.name: Double
characters.art_alt: Double from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Double is a versatile all-rounder who borrows normals and specials from across the cast to adapt her neutral and combo routes.

characters.name: Eliza
characters.art_alt: Eliza from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Eliza has a vast array of offensive tools that make her both a very scary rushdown character when she’s in the opponent’s face, but also play confident in mid-range as well, letting her get in as she pleases.

characters.name: Filia
characters.art_alt: Filia from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Filia is a rushdown pixie character who wants to use her nimble mobility and small size to get in the opponent's face and do brutally fast mixups using her quick, low to the ground air dash.

characters.name: Fukua
characters.art_alt: Fukua from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Fukua plays a space control game with air normals and fireballs, and once she gets a hit, her clones enable very unique and powerful setplay.

characters.name: Marie
characters.art_alt: Marie from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Marie is a gameplay-focused Skullgirls 2nd Encore fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Ms. Fortune
characters.art_alt: Ms. Fortune from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Fortune is a rushdown puppet character who can take off her head, which provides more control in neutral, amazing corner pressure, and unique combos.

characters.name: Painwheel
characters.art_alt: Painwheel from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Painwheel also has a special kind of armor on many of her normals called Hatred Guard, which deals back damage taken to the opponent.

characters.name: Parasoul
characters.art_alt: Parasoul from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Parasoul uses tear-shot projectiles and her Egret assists to control grounded space, while jHK and float movement alter her jump arc for varied approach timing.

characters.name: Peacock
characters.art_alt: Peacock from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: With all her projectiles and runaway tools she can slowly chip away at the opponent's health and build lots of meter in the process.

characters.name: Robo-Fortune
characters.art_alt: Robo-Fortune from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Robo-Fortune is a zoner/keepaway character who uses her amazing mobility, Headrone special moves, and beam projectiles to keep the opponent far away and frustrate them to no end.

characters.name: Squigly
characters.art_alt: Squigly from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Squigly is a midrange character who capitalizes off her opponents mistakes.

characters.name: Umbrella
characters.art_alt: Umbrella from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: When Ravenous , Umbrella's dash, back dash, and dash jump are much quicker than usual, and you have access to her fastest collection of normals, including the fastest normal in the game ( Ravenous 2LP; 4 frame start up).

characters.name: Valentine
characters.art_alt: Valentine from Skullgirls 2nd Encore
characters.description: Valentine's fast airdash normals create close-range pressure, with multi-hit jMP and cross-up jHP giving her strong approach and left-right mix-up options.

characters.name: Bang Shishigami
characters.art_alt: Bang Shishigami from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: In the game, Bang's Drive is Burning Heart - after a brief charge, he launches forward, dealing an attack.

characters.name: Carl Clover
characters.art_alt: Carl Clover from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Carl is a puppet character who controls Nirvana separately from himself, using synchronized attacks to create layered pressure and setplay.

characters.name: Es
characters.art_alt: Es from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: The sword is incredibly sharp, able to easily cut through a Union's crystal, which is otherwise thought to be indestructible.

characters.name: Hakumen
characters.art_alt: Hakumen from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Hakumen has a unique Magatama Gauge , instead of a Heat Gauge, which is used for him to activate his special attacks.

characters.name: Hazama
characters.art_alt: Hazama from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Hazama uses chain-based movement to swing around the screen, control unusual angles, and convert approach hits into tricky pressure.

characters.name: Iron Tager
characters.art_alt: Iron Tager from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: This is reflected in gameplay where his Drive is Voltic Battler - should Tager hit an opponent with his Drive, then certain throws, normals, specials, and Drive attacks will bring his opponents closer.

characters.name: Izayoi
characters.art_alt: Izayoi from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: With intimidation provided by the projectile Sonic Saber and midair movement provided by Mirage Thruster , take control of the pace of the match.

characters.name: Jin Kisaragi
characters.art_alt: Jin Kisaragi from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Jin Kisaragi's mere presence creates snowflakes in the air, and his Drive is Frost Bite.

characters.name: Lambda-11
characters.art_alt: Lambda-11 from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: In Chrono Phantasma Extend , Lambda's Drive was renamed to Sword Summoner EX and had its function changed: while still fundamentally similar, Sword Summoner EX would create an additional projectile automatically after hitting an opponent.

characters.name: Mai Natsume
characters.art_alt: Mai Natsume from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: The rushing skill Himeyuri is just the beginning of several quick attacks in the mid- to close-range that she possesses.

characters.name: Makoto Nanaya
characters.art_alt: Makoto Nanaya from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Makoto Nanaya's in-game Drive is Impact , which allows her to charge her punches to deliver blows of various strengths.

characters.name: Mu-12
characters.art_alt: Mu-12 from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Most of Mu's moves keep her opponent at bay, stopping them in their tracks, although she can boast good close-range pressure and can use Origin to get out of opponent's pressure.

characters.name: Noel Vermillion
characters.art_alt: Noel Vermillion from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Noel is a fast gunner-rushdown character who uses chained drive strings, stance-like routes, and rapid movement to keep pressure active.

characters.name: Platinum the Trinity
characters.art_alt: Platinum the Trinity from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Platinum is a flexible midrange character whose rotating item system changes her pressure, zoning, and combo options from round to round.

characters.name: Rachel Alucard
characters.art_alt: Rachel Alucard from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Rachel Alucard's Drive is further amplified by both her mastery over sorcery and magic , which she often uses to summons bolts of lightning or teleport, on which there seemed to be little limit on how many she could transfer at one point.

characters.name: Ragna the Bloodedge
characters.art_alt: Ragna the Bloodedge from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: It can restore Ragna's health every time he lands a successful Drive attack, absorb the wishes and dreams of the chosen (although his body has to pay a heavy toll to continuously do so), or pull souls from the Susano'o Unit .

characters.name: Relius Clover
characters.art_alt: Relius Clover from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Any Drive input will make Ignis attack, but Relius himself is free to move while she does so.

characters.name: Taokaka
characters.art_alt: Taokaka from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: Tao's Drive , Dancing Edge allows her to dash at lightning speeds and attack an opponent with her razor-sharp claws.

characters.name: Tsubaki Yayoi
characters.art_alt: Tsubaki Yayoi from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: When using Izayoi, Tsubaki is able to fight against most opponents on an even keel, and frequently switches between its whip and sword form for its blade.

characters.name: Valkenhayn R. Hellsing
characters.art_alt: Valkenhayn R. Hellsing from BlazBlue: Continuum Shift Extend
characters.description: In gameplay, Valkenhayn's Drive is Werwolf , which allows him to transform between wolf and human.

characters.name: Abigail
characters.art_alt: Abigail from Street Fighter V
characters.description: With some of the slowest walk speed, slowest dash, and slowest buttons in the game Abigail is not for players looking for an agile character.

characters.name: Akuma
characters.art_alt: Akuma from Street Fighter V
characters.description: The price he pays for this versatility is frighteningly low health and stun, as well as somewhat short range on some of his normals.

characters.name: Alex
characters.art_alt: Alex from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Alex is a patient brawler who uses long pokes and a command grab to frustrate opponents before cashing out on a hard read.

characters.name: Balrog
characters.art_alt: Balrog from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Balrog's V-Skill 1 and Critical Art also allows him to easily deal with projectiles, while his V-Skill 2 lets him make his dash punches multi-hitting and safe, making his approach even easier.

characters.name: Birdie
characters.art_alt: Birdie from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Birdie controls midrange with long cancelable normals, a far-reaching chain grab, and crush-counter buttons that punish careless approaches.

characters.name: Blanka
characters.art_alt: Blanka from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Blanka mixes charge specials, rolling approaches, and ambiguous hops to create unpredictable pressure after getting close.

characters.name: Cammy
characters.art_alt: Cammy from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Cammy is a rushdown, pressure heavy character in it's purest form.

characters.name: Chun-Li
characters.art_alt: Chun-Li from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Chun is your classic "Footsies" character - focusing on a patient neutral game where one attempts to control the space around him, poke in the opponent's space while simultaniously punish the opponent if they get into your space.

characters.name: Dan
characters.art_alt: Dan from Street Fighter V
characters.description: They allow him to expand his combo and pressure possibilities in different ways, including his damage potential, while also allowing him to build his v-meter securely.

characters.name: Dhalsim
characters.art_alt: Dhalsim from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Dhalsim is a gameplay-focused Street Fighter V fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: E. Honda
characters.art_alt: E. Honda from Street Fighter V
characters.description: The constant threat of his command grab and armor breaking VT1 only adds to his pressure.

characters.name: Ed
characters.art_alt: Ed from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Ed is a gameplay-focused Street Fighter V fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Eleven
characters.art_alt: Eleven from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Special Course: Hyper Street Fighter II Combo Chronicle Vol.

characters.name: F.A.N.G
characters.art_alt: F.A.N.G from Street Fighter V
characters.description: F.A.N.G. uses poison-coated specials, traps, and slippery movement to control space and make every blocked approach costly.

characters.name: Falke
characters.art_alt: Falke from Street Fighter V
characters.description: If you like long ranged normals and don't crack under pressure, Falke is a good choice.

characters.name: G
characters.art_alt: G from Street Fighter V
characters.description: G is a momentum-based, rushdown fighter with an oppressive ground game and excels at opening up opponents with good frame traps and normals, while also always threatening with a command grab.

characters.name: Gill
characters.art_alt: Gill from Street Fighter V
characters.description: If Gill puts the opponent in a freezing or burning state and then hits them with a move utilizing the opposite element (ice move while burning, fire move while freezing), then his combo ability goes up exponentially.

characters.name: Guile
characters.art_alt: Guile from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Guile is a gameplay-focused Street Fighter V fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Ibuki
characters.art_alt: Ibuki from Street Fighter V
characters.description: At the start of the round, Ibuki has access to 6 Kunai that can be thrown like a projectile on the ground, in the air, or released all at once for extended combos.

characters.name: Juri
characters.art_alt: Juri from Street Fighter V
characters.description: The LK version is a slow moving fireball, the MK version is an jumping attack that leads to longer combo opportunities, and the HK version is a forward moving attack used mostly as a combo ender.

characters.name: Kage
characters.art_alt: Kage from Street Fighter V
characters.description: One of his most notable attributes is his advantage after his forward throw, as he's +9 within poking range; compared to many other characters, Kage is much better at continuing offensive pressure after throwing the opponent.

characters.name: Karin
characters.art_alt: Karin from Street Fighter V
characters.description: On top of this, she has excellent mid pokes in 5MK and 5HK to keep the opponent sitting still at her preferred ranges, a great tick throw from 5LK , and long-range whiff punishes with 2HK .

characters.name: Ken
characters.art_alt: Ken from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Ken has a slowish fireball and bad pokes, but instead has great corner carry, great mobility, solid damage and some of the better v-meter building in the game.

characters.name: Kolin
characters.art_alt: Kolin from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Kolin is a counter-focused midrange fighter who uses parries, ice attacks, and freeze-based V-Trigger setups to punish predictable offense.

characters.name: Laura
characters.art_alt: Laura from Street Fighter V
characters.description: While her buttons are not the longest range, many such as stand LK and 2MP have great priority that can make counter poking effective and lead into Bolt Charge and lets her start her mixups.

characters.name: Lucia
characters.art_alt: Lucia from Street Fighter V
characters.description: When she scores a solid hit, her corner carry is very respectable, and both of her triggers enhance it further; VT2 is essentially capable of meterless corner-to-corner carry on a crush counter activation combo, which is very strong for a 2-bar trigger.

characters.name: Luke
characters.art_alt: Luke from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Luke is an all-around brawler who combines advancing punches, sand blasts, and charged specials for stable neutral and strong corner carry.

characters.name: M. Bison
characters.art_alt: M. Bison from Street Fighter V
characters.description: When he gets close, his gameplan starts to shine, as he has many options to maintain advantage on block and excellent throw range to make up for his poor walkspeed; getting bison away from you often requires good abare, and his explosive damage makes that abare very risky.

characters.name: Menat
characters.art_alt: Menat from Street Fighter V
characters.description: After Menat places the orb on screen, all of her punch normals and HK normals will be changed with "orbless" versions, usually resulting in less range but better frame advantage for better combo opportunities.

characters.name: Nash
characters.art_alt: Nash from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Nash is all about being in the right spacing, for all purposes - spacing his long range pokes properly, spacing his v-skill activation position, spacing his anti airs properly, spacing his sonic boom throwing and offensive followups, etc.

characters.name: Oro
characters.art_alt: Oro from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Oro is a gameplay-focused Street Fighter V fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Poison
characters.art_alt: Poison from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Poison controls midrange with her long whip, projectiles, and counter-pokes before converting a clean hit into corner pressure.

characters.name: R. Mika
characters.art_alt: R. Mika from Street Fighter V
characters.description: R. Mika loves harassing the opponent with her great normals, a command grab that loops into itself, and great mobility.

characters.name: Rashid
characters.art_alt: Rashid from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Rashid is a mobile rushdown fighter who uses whirlwind projectiles, wall movement, and airborne approaches to force rapid side-switching pressure.

characters.name: Rose
characters.art_alt: Rose from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Rose is a technical space-control fighter who uses Soul Spheres, projectile defense, and V-Trigger setups to dictate neutral.

characters.name: Ryu
characters.art_alt: Ryu from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Ryu has more than solid tools for nearly everything - zoning capabilities, pressure and mixup options, poking, anti airing and frame trapping, corner carry and damage, as well as defensive options.

characters.name: Sagat
characters.art_alt: Sagat from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Sagat is a gameplay-focused Street Fighter V fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Sakura
characters.art_alt: Sakura from Street Fighter V
characters.description: With a quick walk-speed and dash, she can "shimmy" well and keep up the pressure and chase her fireballs.

characters.name: Seth
characters.art_alt: Seth from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Seth's VS1 can alter his frame traps and block strings utilizing Install Arts to make the opponent second guess themselves about what to do after, and both of his V-Triggers have great damage output and setups to make Seth even more scary than he already is.

characters.name: Urien
characters.art_alt: Urien from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Because of his slow walk speed, long dashes, and status as a four-frame character with high-startup normals, Urien must attempt to make hard read (as with an anti-air fireball), force a scramble (EX Headbutt while at disadvantage), or create a mixup sequence to get rolling.

characters.name: Vega
characters.art_alt: Vega from Street Fighter V
characters.description: While in no claw, Vega has access to different punch normals and different special moves losing Aurora Spin edge but gaining a command grab.

characters.name: Zangief
characters.art_alt: Zangief from Street Fighter V
characters.description: Zangief is a command-grab grappler who conditions opponents with armored approaches, powerful normals, and devastating SPD throws.

characters.name: Zeku
characters.art_alt: Zeku from Street Fighter V
characters.description: The old form excels at long ranged spacing and poking, while the young form is better at pressure and combos.

characters.name: Akuma
characters.art_alt: Akuma from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3, Akuma is a simple but effective character who runs away while harassing with aerial fireballs and trying to snipe opponents with his fast beam hyper.

characters.name: Amaterasu
characters.art_alt: Amaterasu from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Ammy can switch weapons at any time she can perform a special move, by using her 22X Weapon Change Special.

characters.name: Arthur
characters.art_alt: Arthur from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3 , Arthur is a projectile-heavy keepaway character who uses a variety of long range special moves to deal significant chip damage to opponents while keeping them locked down.

characters.name: C. Viper
characters.art_alt: C. Viper from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In addition to a normal dash, double jump, and 8-Way airdash Viper has several additional movement options.

characters.name: Chris Redfield
characters.art_alt: Chris Redfield from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3 , Chris is a midrange or keepaway-focused character with limited mobility but strong damage output.

characters.name: Chun-Li
characters.art_alt: Chun-Li from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Chun can combine this with her other aerial movement tools, including Spinning Bird Kick, Tenshokyaku, and her Walljump, to stay very evasive in the air.

characters.name: Dante
characters.art_alt: Dante from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3, Dante is a highly technical character sporting the longest list of special moves in the game.

characters.name: Deadpool
characters.art_alt: Deadpool from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3, Deadpool is an obnoxious keepaway character who tries to keep his distance in neutral while harassing with his very fast Trigger Happy (236X) gunshot special.

characters.name: Doctor Doom
characters.art_alt: Doctor Doom from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: If this sequence was done quickly enough that the opponent is still in blockstun, or tried to jump out of pressure, Doom will then attack with a 6H High Kick, which can itself be Triangle Jump canceled to continue the offensive.

characters.name: Dormammu
characters.art_alt: Dormammu from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Dormammu's grounded dash is a fixed duration "hop"-style dash.

characters.name: Felicia
characters.art_alt: Felicia from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Although she lacks traditional aerial mobility and has poor range, Felicia is very fast and has several tools to go for mixups and resets once she closes in on her opponent.

characters.name: Firebrand
characters.art_alt: Firebrand from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: The combination of a Wall Cling, a threatening dive kick style move in Bon Voyage (236S), a unique command air dash in Hell's Elevator (214X), a flight mode, and a install that grants him a 25% speed boost in Luminous Body (214XX) makes Firebrand difficult to catch and even more difficult to avoid.

characters.name: Frank West
characters.art_alt: Frank West from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Experience is gained by taking pictures using Frank's 236S special, which has a large range and also hits OTG.

characters.name: Ghost Rider
characters.art_alt: Ghost Rider from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3, Ghost Rider is a keepaway-focused character.

characters.name: Hawkeye
characters.art_alt: Hawkeye from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Hawkeye is a keepaway specialist who uses fullscreen arrows, Trick Maneuver movement, and fast hypers to control space and punish approaches.

characters.name: Hulk
characters.art_alt: Hulk from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Hulk's grounded dash is a fixed duration "hop"-style dash.

characters.name: Iron Fist
characters.art_alt: Iron Fist from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: However, he has virtually no ranged abilities, almost no aerial mobility or aerial attack capabilities, and limited defensive tools.

characters.name: Iron Man
characters.art_alt: Iron Man from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: With both an 8-way airdash and a flight mode, Iron Man can run away from opponents or even go on the offensive with some nasty high/low mixups.

characters.name: Jill Valentine
characters.art_alt: Jill Valentine from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Additionally, she has Mad Beast (214XX), a fairly unique 3-Bar install that puts her into a stance of sorts in which she can freely use normals, her teleport becomes much more versatile and threatening, and she gains additional hitstun.

characters.name: Magneto
characters.art_alt: Magneto from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: While Magneto lacks a clearly definable character archtype in UMVC3, he has movement options that allow him to weave around opponent's attacks with fast airdashes and flight.

characters.name: Mike Haggar
characters.art_alt: Mike Haggar from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Typical of characters in his archtype, Haggar is fairly slow compared to the cast as a whole, and can struggle to approach opponents with strong keepaway tools.

characters.name: Morrigan
characters.art_alt: Morrigan from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Additionally, Morrigan can cancel the airborne frames on incoming of Cross-over Counter into flight.

characters.name: Nemesis
characters.art_alt: Nemesis from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Nemesis can attack enemies from a distance with extended tentacle attacks and his rocket launcher, before approaching with a surprisingly fast ground dash.

characters.name: Nova
characters.art_alt: Nova from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3 , Nova is an all-rounder with good mobility and a variety of tools for both keepaway and rushdown.

characters.name: Phoenix
characters.art_alt: Phoenix from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Phoenix zones opponents out using her 236X "TK Shot" projectiles and 214X "TK Trap" specials to control space while maneuvering around the stage with Flight and a fast 8-way airdash.

characters.name: Phoenix Wright
characters.art_alt: Phoenix Wright from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Phoenix's moveset in Turnabout Mode is similar to his Trial Mode, but many of his attacks are greatly enhanced, with extended range, damage, and properties.

characters.name: Rocket Raccoon
characters.art_alt: Rocket Raccoon from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Rocket Raccoon can cancel float at any time by letting go of up, or by using any attack or aerial special.

characters.name: She-Hulk
characters.art_alt: She-Hulk from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: She-Hulk has access to a crouching stance (Runner's Start), a running stance (Chariot) and an airborne stance (Catapult).

characters.name: Shuma-Gorath
characters.art_alt: Shuma-Gorath from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Shuma has historically been an unpopular character due to his technical requirements and awkward movement, but he brings many powerful mixup tools and an incredible assist to players who master him.

characters.name: Spencer
characters.art_alt: Spencer from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Spencer's Wire Grapple M (Slant Shot) assist uniquely provides a way for characters to restand airborne opponents, leading to many combo extensions and resets that are only possible with Spencer.

characters.name: Spider-Man
characters.art_alt: Spider-Man from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Second, his Ultimate Web Throw hyper (63214XX) is an anti-air command grab with massive range that can be followed up with a combo if it connects.

characters.name: Storm
characters.art_alt: Storm from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: A Storm player must either activate float below the minimum airdash height, or space their inputs far enough apart to not be interpreted as airdash.

characters.name: Strider Hiryu
characters.art_alt: Strider Hiryu from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: This drastically improves Strider's High/Low mixup game by allowing him to perform fast Instant Overhead attacks and then convert them solo into a combo or additional block pressure.

characters.name: Super-Skrull
characters.art_alt: Super-Skrull from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Super-Skrull can also perform hit/throw mixups or even guard breaks from a long range by combining his long-range normals and command normals with his 214X command grab.

characters.name: Taskmaster
characters.art_alt: Taskmaster from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Taskmaster is slow - both his mobility and his attacks have poor speed, but he has solid range on his sword attacks and a versatile moveset.

characters.name: Thor
characters.art_alt: Thor from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Thor has a slow - but powerful - beam, as well as specials with projectile nullification or even armor, which when paired with his huge health pool (the largest in the game), can be used to bully his way toward opponents.

characters.name: Trish
characters.art_alt: Trish from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: In UMvC3, Trish is a relatively straightforward character who maneuvers around the screen with flight and an 8-way airdash while poking with her projectiles and fishing for normal hits to convert into a combo.

characters.name: Tron Bonne
characters.art_alt: Tron Bonne from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Although she has several long-range and projectile attacks, these are primarily used to extend combos or support her primary goal of approaching the opponent to open them up with a throw or high/low mixup.

characters.name: Vergil
characters.art_alt: Vergil from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Vergil can not special-cancel his normal attacks on whiff, unless he is in his Devil Trigger (214XX) install.

characters.name: Viewtiful Joe
characters.art_alt: Viewtiful Joe from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: It would be more accurate to describe this mechanic as having two Air Actions, since Joe also has an airdash he can spend his air actions on.

characters.name: Wesker
characters.art_alt: Wesker from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Wesker can use these to augment a harassing, keepaway style with his Samurai Edge gunshot command normals, or an aggressive, rushdown style with fast normal attacks and a strong command grab special.

characters.name: Wolverine
characters.art_alt: Wolverine from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: While lacking long-ranged attacks or projectiles of any kind, he can quickly close in with his fast ground dash and aerial divekick.

characters.name: X-23
characters.art_alt: X-23 from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: X-23 has Talon Attack (j.236X) which is a unique movement option and attack that she can cancel any normal or special that leaves her airborne.

characters.name: Zero
characters.art_alt: Zero from Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3
characters.description: Zero is also infamous for his ability to OTG relaunch with just about any assist in the game, and for his "Lightning Loops" combos, which allow him to kill any character with very good meter efficiency.

characters.name: Bedman
characters.art_alt: Bedman from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Bedman's variety of movement options, solid normals and boomerang-style projectile gives Bedman the ability to play evasive until he can set up Deja-Vu and take control of the match, but if he's caught off guard his defensive options are limited.

characters.name: Chipp Zanuff
characters.art_alt: Chipp Zanuff from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Guilty Gear's dedicated pixie character with great mobility and paper-thin defense.

characters.name: Elphelt Valentine
characters.art_alt: Elphelt Valentine from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Elphelt is a versatile character who has multiple weapons to get her opponents at any position.

characters.name: Faust
characters.art_alt: Faust from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Faust is a spacing specialist who uses long normals, random items, and strong air attacks to control neutral and keep opponents at bay.

characters.name: I-No
characters.art_alt: I-No from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: I-No is a gameplay-focused GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN- fighter whose neutral tools, pressure routes, and conversions define the character's gameplan.

characters.name: Jack-O'
characters.art_alt: Jack-O' from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Jack-O uses Dust servants as special moves, giving her low-profile overheads, a command grab, a divekick, and airborne projectiles for setplay pressure.

characters.name: Johnny
characters.art_alt: Johnny from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Learning to use Mist Finer well gives Johnny fantastic range in neutral, allowing him to poke and counterzone with the best of them.

characters.name: Ky Kiske
characters.art_alt: Ky Kiske from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Ky excels at confirming knockdown from ground gatlings, and also greatly benefits from the reworked meter system, giving him useful options with enough tension.

characters.name: Leo Whitefang
characters.art_alt: Leo Whitefang from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Leo Whitefang's moveset revolves around close-ranged pressure and his unique Brynhildr stance, where he turns his back on the enemy.

characters.name: May
characters.art_alt: May from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: May is a pressure-oriented midrange fighter who uses charged dolphins, large normals, and beach-ball setplay to force approaches and frame traps.

characters.name: Millia Rage
characters.art_alt: Millia Rage from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Millia is a high speed rushdown character who thrives off of her terrifyingly strong high/low mixup potential.

characters.name: Potemkin
characters.art_alt: Potemkin from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Potemkin uses short blockstrings combined with approaching moves like Hammerfall to overwhelm and confuse his opponent, then punish their reaction to his pressure.

characters.name: Ramlethal Valentine
characters.art_alt: Ramlethal Valentine from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Ramlethal controls midrange with two giant swords, placing them independently for extended blockstrings, setplay, and corner pressure.

characters.name: Raven
characters.art_alt: Raven from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Supporting all this are some weird but powerful movement options: a fast, invisible, invulnerable run and an airborne glide he can cancel out of for unreactable high-low mixups.

characters.name: Sin Kiske
characters.art_alt: Sin Kiske from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Sin is a long-range pressure fighter whose hunger meter must be managed between combos while he uses strong mids and simple mixups.

characters.name: Slayer
characters.art_alt: Slayer from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Many of his attacks specialize in invulnerability, mixup, and counter hits, spreading doubt and confusion in the opponent's mind.

characters.name: Sol Badguy
characters.art_alt: Sol Badguy from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: While lacking a strong, standing overhead, much of Sol’s close-range mix-up comes from his command throw, Bukkirabou ni Nageru, and the fear of getting caught in his command throw opening the opponent up to frame traps.

characters.name: Venom
characters.art_alt: Venom from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Venom is an advanced character, you'll have to learn his unique neutral game as well as play strong defense, for he has no reversal (even with meter), but when you put his gameplan together, he is a versatile character who is immensely satisfying to play!

characters.name: Zato-1
characters.art_alt: Zato-1 from GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN-
characters.description: Together along with Eddie, the shadow, he dominates in neutral along with his overwhelming offensive.

characters.name: Amane Nishiki
characters.art_alt: Amane Nishiki from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Kato: Since it had already been decided from the start that Amane would use his sash/obi for long-range attacks, I designed him so that it could be removed smoothly.

characters.name: Azrael
characters.art_alt: Azrael from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Azrael's Drive is The Terror - each time he hits an opponent with his Drive, he exposes a weak point and additional Drive hits cause greater damage.

characters.name: Bang Shishigami
characters.art_alt: Bang Shishigami from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: In the game, Bang's Drive is Burning Heart - after a brief charge, he launches forward, dealing an attack.

characters.name: Bullet
characters.art_alt: Bullet from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: When the opponent is in this circle and the Drive button is released, Bullet will launch herself at the opponent and grab them, although this grab functions like a normal move and not a command grab.

characters.name: Carl Clover
characters.art_alt: Carl Clover from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Carl is a puppet character who controls Nirvana separately from himself, using synchronized attacks to create layered pressure and setplay.

characters.name: Celica A. Mercury
characters.art_alt: Celica A. Mercury from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: In Central Fiction , Celica will build a blue health bar on top of her current health whenever she lands a Drive combo, and can opt to "heal", making that blue health into health proper instead of using a special move.

characters.name: Es
characters.art_alt: Es from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: The sword is incredibly sharp, able to easily cut through a Union's crystal, which is otherwise thought to be indestructible.

characters.name: Hakumen
characters.art_alt: Hakumen from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Hakumen has a unique Magatama Gauge , instead of a Heat Gauge, which is used for him to activate his special attacks.

characters.name: Hazama
characters.art_alt: Hazama from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Hazama uses chain-based movement to swing around the screen, control unusual angles, and convert approach hits into tricky pressure.

characters.name: Hibiki Kohaku
characters.art_alt: Hibiki Kohaku from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Should the need arise, he can use his Drive Double Chase , and create a shadow clone of himself as a distraction so he can move in for the kill with his twin blades - both of which he wields with deadly accuracy and intricate skill.

characters.name: Iron Tager
characters.art_alt: Iron Tager from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: This is reflected in gameplay where his Drive is Voltic Battler - should Tager hit an opponent with his Drive, then certain throws, normals, specials, and Drive attacks will bring his opponents closer.

characters.name: Izayoi
characters.art_alt: Izayoi from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: With intimidation provided by the projectile Sonic Saber and midair movement provided by Mirage Thruster , take control of the pace of the match.

characters.name: Jin Kisaragi
characters.art_alt: Jin Kisaragi from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Jin Kisaragi's mere presence creates snowflakes in the air, and his Drive is Frost Bite.

characters.name: Kagura Mutsuki
characters.art_alt: Kagura Mutsuki from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Kagura's weapon is an enormous black sword with red grooves along both edges.

characters.name: Kokonoe
characters.art_alt: Kokonoe from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: During a fight, her in game Drive is Graviton , which allows the control of gravity with a small device; however, these only last so long.

characters.name: Lambda-11
characters.art_alt: Lambda-11 from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: In Chrono Phantasma Extend , Lambda's Drive was renamed to Sword Summoner EX and had its function changed: while still fundamentally similar, Sword Summoner EX would create an additional projectile automatically after hitting an opponent.

characters.name: Mai Natsume
characters.art_alt: Mai Natsume from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: The rushing skill Himeyuri is just the beginning of several quick attacks in the mid- to close-range that she possesses.

characters.name: Makoto Nanaya
characters.art_alt: Makoto Nanaya from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Makoto Nanaya's in-game Drive is Impact , which allows her to charge her punches to deliver blows of various strengths.

characters.name: Mu-12
characters.art_alt: Mu-12 from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Most of Mu's moves keep her opponent at bay, stopping them in their tracks, although she can boast good close-range pressure and can use Origin to get out of opponent's pressure.

characters.name: Nine the Phantom
characters.art_alt: Nine the Phantom from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Nine the Phantom is capable of short-range teleportation in battle as well as ability to dispel other's spells cast upon her.

characters.name: Noel Vermillion
characters.art_alt: Noel Vermillion from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Noel is a fast gunner-rushdown character who uses chained drive strings, stance-like routes, and rapid movement to keep pressure active.

characters.name: Platinum the Trinity
characters.art_alt: Platinum the Trinity from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Platinum is a flexible midrange character whose rotating item system changes her pressure, zoning, and combo options from round to round.

characters.name: Rachel Alucard
characters.art_alt: Rachel Alucard from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Rachel Alucard's Drive is further amplified by both her mastery over sorcery and magic , which she often uses to summons bolts of lightning or teleport, on which there seemed to be little limit on how many she could transfer at one point.

characters.name: Ragna the Bloodedge
characters.art_alt: Ragna the Bloodedge from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: It can restore Ragna's health every time he lands a successful Drive attack, absorb the wishes and dreams of the chosen (although his body has to pay a heavy toll to continuously do so), or pull souls from the Susano'o Unit .

characters.name: Relius Clover
characters.art_alt: Relius Clover from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Any Drive input will make Ignis attack, but Relius himself is free to move while she does so.

characters.name: Taokaka
characters.art_alt: Taokaka from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Tao's Drive , Dancing Edge allows her to dash at lightning speeds and attack an opponent with her razor-sharp claws.

characters.name: Terumi
characters.art_alt: Terumi from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: Instead of eating the opponent's lifebar, Terumi's Drive grants him copious amounts of Heat upon a successful hit, and to reflect this, most of his moves are Distortion Drives .

characters.name: Tsubaki Yayoi
characters.art_alt: Tsubaki Yayoi from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: When using Izayoi, Tsubaki is able to fight against most opponents on an even keel, and frequently switches between its whip and sword form for its blade.

characters.name: Valkenhayn R. Hellsing
characters.art_alt: Valkenhayn R. Hellsing from BlazBlue: Chronophantasma Extend
characters.description: In gameplay, Valkenhayn's Drive is Werwolf , which allows him to transform between wolf and human.

characters.name: Answer
characters.art_alt: Answer from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Answer is a flexible offense-focused character that uses tricky movement, great normals, and unique setups to overwhelm his opponent.

characters.name: Axl Low
characters.art_alt: Axl Low from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: While his chains may remind you of Street Fighter's Dhalsim, he has some tools to pressure opponents at close range as well.

characters.name: Baiken
characters.art_alt: Baiken from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Capable of wildly swinging the course of a match with a successful guard cancel that leads into reliable okizeme and dangerous mixup, Baiken is a credible threat with huge potential for massive comebacks.

characters.name: Bedman
characters.art_alt: Bedman from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Bedman places seals with special moves and replays them as delayed attacks, turning screen space into layered setplay pressure.

characters.name: Chipp Zanuff
characters.art_alt: Chipp Zanuff from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Off of throw or another good knockdown, Chipp can often set up a jump-in mixup using j.

characters.name: Dizzy
characters.art_alt: Dizzy from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Dizzy controls space with summoned fish and seals, then uses those setplay tools to create layered high-low and left-right pressure.

characters.name: Elphelt Valentine
characters.art_alt: Elphelt Valentine from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Elphelt is a versatile stance character who has many tools for different situations.

characters.name: Faust
characters.art_alt: Faust from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Faust is a fundamentals based spacing character who aims to dominate neutral via long/range normals and items thrown with item toss 23 He also rules the skies with very good air normals, making it very difficult for the opponent to find an opening, even without being hampered by items.

characters.name: I-No
characters.art_alt: I-No from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: I-No is a mixup monster, whose strength lies in her unique Morrigan-style hoverdash that leaves her airborne, allowing her to use her aerial overhead moves very low to the ground.

characters.name: Jack-O'
characters.art_alt: Jack-O' from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Jack-O uses Dust servants as special moves, giving her low-profile overheads, a command grab, a divekick, and airborne projectiles for setplay pressure.

characters.name: Jam Kuradoberi
characters.art_alt: Jam Kuradoberi from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: The ki-wielding fighting chef Jam is a highly-mobile rushdown queen with scary close-range pressure and high damage off openings.

characters.name: Johnny
characters.art_alt: Johnny from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Learning to use Mist Finer well gives Johnny fantastic range in neutral, allowing him to poke and counterzone with the best of them.

characters.name: Kum Haehyun
characters.art_alt: Kum Haehyun from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: However, Haehyun's neutral and movement are extremely linear compared to most other characters.

characters.name: Ky Kiske
characters.art_alt: Ky Kiske from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
characters.description: Ky controls neutral and okizeme with Stun Edge projectiles, then converts corner hits into sword pressure and wall-splat combos.

characters.name: Leo Whitefang
characters.art_alt: Leo Whitefang from GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2
